Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

State the evidence-based conclusions about production and customer demand, and keep the sheet focused on the run evidence rather than making or reopening a menu decision.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Roasted-chicken sale runs — decision evidence", "body": "# Roasted-chicken sale runs — decision evidence

**Scope:** Evidence from the three controlled 30-pound sale runs only. This sheet records production and customer demand; it does not make or reopen a menu decision.

| Run | Production evidence | Customer demand and disposition | Contribution after food and incremental labor* |
|---|---|---|---:|
| June 28 | 19 lb 12 oz cooked (316 oz); 45 complete 7-oz portions + 1 oz; 57 incremental labor min; tested sequence unchanged. **Met** ≤60 min / ≥44 portions. | 45 prepared; 43 sold (95.6%); 2 chilled for staff meal. | $605.20 |
| July 26 | 44 complete portions; 59 incremental labor min; tested sequence used. **Met** ≤60 min / ≥44 portions. | 44 prepared; 40 sold (90.9%); 4 handled as staff meal. | $550.40 |
| August 16 | 45 complete portions; 56 incremental labor min; tested sequence used. **Met** ≤60 min / ≥44 portions. | 45 prepared; 44 sold (97.8%); 1 retained for staff meal. | $623.60 |

## Evidence-based conclusions

- **Production:** The unchanged case size and tested pre-staging/tray sequence produced 44–45 complete portions in all three sale runs, with 56–59 incremental labor minutes. Every run met both controls: no more than 60 labor minutes and at least 44 complete portions. The observed results support repeatability under these tested conditions.
- **Demand:** Sales were 40–44 plates per run; sell-through ranged from 90.9% to 97.8%. Across the runs, 127 of 134 prepared plates sold (94.8%). Demand was strong in these services but varied; the unsold portions were staff-meal disposition, not customer demand.
- **Economics:** Using $146 food cost per run and $24/hour incremental labor valuation, recorded contribution after those costs ranged from $550.40 to $623.60. This is contribution after food and incremental labor, not full profit.

\* June: $774 revenue − $146 food cost − $22.80 labor. July: $720 − $146 − $23.60.
